equation_request.abstract: We present an algebraic framework to study the time-optimal synthesis of arbitrary unitaries in $SU(2)$, when the control set is restricted to rotations around two non-parallel axes in the Bloch sphere. Our method bypasses commonly used control-theoretical techniques, and easily imposes necessary conditions on time-optimal sequences. In a straightforward fashion, we prove that time-optimal sequences are solely parametrized by three rotation angles and derive general bounds on those angles as a function of the relative rotation speed of each control and the angle between the axes. Results are substantially different whether both clockwise and counterclockwise rotations about the given axes are allowed, or only clockwise rotations. In the first case, we prove that any finite time-optimal sequence is composed at most of five control concatenations, while for the more restrictive case, we present scaling laws on the maximum length of any finite time-optimal sequence. The bounds we find for both cases are stricter than previously published ones and severely constrain the structure of time-optimal sequences, allowing for an efficient numerical search of the time-optimal solution. Our results can be used to find the time-optimal evolution of qubit systems under the action of the considered control set, and thus potentially increase the number of realizable unitaries before decoherence.

specification.problem: Given a classical single-qubit target U in SU(2) and two non-parallel rotation controls (Rz at rate 1, Rn about n=(sin theta,0,cos theta) at rate r), find a minimum-time sequence of control rotations whose product equals U up to global phase, and build it as a one-qubit circuit.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One qubit, no ancilla, no black box, no measurement (statevector/unitary read). Only the five-segment Euler-like form Rz(a1)Rn(b1)Rz(a2)Rn(b2)Rz(a3) is built, with three free angles, plus a classical bounded grid or optimizer search over those angles. The paper's specific angle bounds, the five-concatenation proof and the clockwise-only length scaling laws are outside scope and not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: angle between the Rz axis and the second axis n in the xz-plane
relative rotation speed of Rn versus Rz
total control time of a sequence

equations.label: Axis rotation
equations.description: Implements rotation about n using standard gates; Ry(theta) maps z to n.
equations.justification: Standard frame change; sign convention of Ry should be checked in simulation so that Ry(theta) takes z to n.
assumptions: n lies in the xz-plane at angle theta from z

equations.label: Five-segment decomposition
equations.description: Time-optimal sequences are parametrized by three angles; at most five alternating segments when both rotation directions are allowed.
equations.abstract_quote: any finite time-optimal sequence is composed at most of five control concatenations
equations.justification: Five concatenations is the stated maximum. The specific form with three free angles is inferred from 'parametrized by three rotation angles' and is not stated explicitly. Which three angles are free is not given.
assumptions: The ordering and which angles are free are assumed

equations.label: Total time
equations.description: Cost function: Rz at rate 1, Rn at rate r. For clockwise-only, angles are taken in [0,2\pi) so the absolute values are dropped.
equations.justification: Follows from the constant-speed assumption and the relative speed ratio r mentioned in the abstract; the exact definition of r is assumed.
assumptions: r multiplies the Rn angular rate

equations.label: Search problem
equations.description: Bounded numerical search over the angle box B. The bounds come from the paper's results, which are not recoverable here.
equations.abstract_quote: allowing for an efficient numerical search of the time-optimal solution
equations.justification: The abstract says the bounds constrain the structure so a numerical search is efficient. The box B itself is not given; the default is [0,2\pi) per angle.
assumptions: Default box [0,2\pi) per angle if the true bounds are unknown

registers.name: q
registers.role: single qubit on which the control sequence acts

specification.initial_state: |0> (the unitary is read from the circuit, so the input state is irrelevant)

steps.description: Classically compute the target U and set theta and r.
Search the bounded angles for the minimum T with F=1, using a grid or optimizer with random restarts.

Build the circuit by applying rz(a1), the Rn gate (ry(theta) rz(b1) ry(-theta)), rz(a2), Rn(b2), rz(a3) in time order, skipping zero-angle gates. Qiskit applies gates in circuit order, so the matrix product is the reverse of the circuit order.
Read the unitary, compare with U up to global phase, and report T.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute F from the simulated unitary and report T for the optimal angles. Keep the shortest-T solution among those with F near 1 (e.g. above 1-1e-8).
assumptions: Second axis in the xz-plane at angle theta from z
Rates are constant, with ratio r
Both-direction case allows signed angles; the clockwise-only case uses angles in [0,2pi)
Equality is judged up to global phase
Search is a classical grid or optimizer
Five-segment form used as the parametrization
missing_information: The explicit angle bounds as functions of theta and r
Which three angles are the free parameters and the closed-form solution
Scaling-law constants for the clockwise-only maximum length
Whether shorter sequences than five segments need separate handling
